headline: DW has asked two legal experts whether laws written after World War II can still govern AI-powered weapons in modern warfare.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: only DW's short description of the video could be read, so the experts' arguments are unverified.
importance_line: Civilians in war zones and the armies that use AI-assisted weapons are affected by how the laws of war are applied, but this is a discussion of whether the rules fit, not a new rule or ruling.
summary: DW's video discussion, with Bonnie Docherty of Harvard Law School and Human Rights Watch and Laurie R. Blank of Emory University School of Law, asks whether laws written after World War II can still regulate warfare now that militaries use AI to analyse intelligence, identify targets and support battlefield operations.
notes: Video programme; only DW's page description was readable, not the experts' actual arguments. DW gives the two guests' affiliations but not their job titles, so none were added.
